body.text: The initiator is a blockage of fuel subchannels or another localized fault in the core during full power operation, resulting in fuel damage.
body.anchor: a blockage of fuel subchannels or other localized faults within the reactor core

body.text: Partial flow blockage is evaluated because of the tight pin spacing, high power density, and high burnup of sodium fast reactor assemblies.
body.anchor: namely the tight spacing of fuel pins, high power density, and high burnup

items: Debris circulated in the primary sodium
Swelling or bowing of the fuel pins
body.anchor: may be initiated due to an accumulation of debris

body.text: The assumption that an entire assembly failed is conservative and deterministic.
body.anchor: The assumption that an entire fuel assembly failed due to the event is conservative

checks.q: Which is a stated cause of partial flow blockage?
checks.x: Causes are debris, failed wire-wrapped spacers, and swelling or bowing of pins.

body.text: The event challenges cladding, so retention depends on the barriers past the fuel. Functional containment barriers perform their functions, but a release occurs.

title: Local Fuel Fault DBEs
subject: event
intro: A local fuel fault damages fuel without moving bulk plant parameters. Operators, not automatic trips, end this event.

objectives.text: State the event initiator and safety-analysis assumptions.
Identify the challenged safety functions and acceptance criteria.
Recognize the event from alarms and indications.
Select and apply the appropriate procedure.
Respond to failure of an automatic or mitigating function.
Establish and verify the required end state.
Explain the consequences of delayed or incorrect actions.
Relate operator actions to the event's technical basis.
